title: Primitive values and references (intro)
learningObjectives: Explain primitive values and references (intro) and use JavaScript values and operators predictably.

understand.concept: Primitive values are copied as values when assigned or passed. Objects are reference values: assigning an object to another variable copies the reference, so both variables can refer to the same object. Mutating through one reference can be observed through the other.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding references prevents unexpected shared mutations. It also prepares learners for object copying, arrays, function arguments, and state management.
understand.analogy: A primitive assignment copies a value; an object assignment copies a reference to a shared object.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript coercion, equality, and reference semantics follow the language specification.

explain.narrative: Changing second.score changes the same object seen through first. Reassigning b does not change the primitive value held by a.

examples.explanation: Changing second.score changes the same object seen through first. Reassigning b does not change the primitive value held by a.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the values and results described.

practise.guidedTask: Create two variables that refer to one object and two variables holding a primitive. Predict the outputs before running the code.
practise.independentTask: Write a short program using the concept with realistic values. Predict the output before running it and explain any surprising result.
hints: Inspect both value and typeof when needed.
Use explicit conversion and validate its result.
Avoid relying on implicit coercion in security-sensitive logic.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Primitive values and references (intro)</title></head><body>
<script>const first={score:10};const second=first;second.score=20;console.log(first.score);const a=5;let b=a;b=9;console.log(a,b);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: When one variable is assigned an object variable, what is copied?
questions.explanation: The reference is copied, so both variables can refer to the same object.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable way to understand a value conversion?
options: Inspect the original value, converted value, and conversion result
questions.answer: Inspect the original value, converted value, and conversion result
questions.explanation: Explicitly checking conversion results prevents invalid values from silently entering later calculations.
